planets.name: CoRoT-2 b
planets.description: Transiting planet of CoRoT-2 with a 1.74-day year, found in 2008.

text.card: CoRoT-2 b was found in 2008 by CoRoT as it crossed its star.
text.introduction: It is the only planet known around CoRoT-2. Its orbit and size follow Gillon et al. 2010's fit, the archive's default.
text.locator: NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table, default parameter set (pl_refname GILLON_ET_AL__2010): disc_year 2008, disc_facility CoRoT, sy_pnum 1; pl_orbper 1.74299845482, pl_radj 1.466, pl_bmassj 3.47

quotes.title: CoRoT-2b
quotes.card: CoRoT-2b is the second extrasolar planet to be detected by the French-led CoRoT mission, and orbits the star CoRoT-2 at a distance of 700 light-years from Earth towards the constellation Aquila.
quotes.introduction: Its discovery was announced on 20 December 2007.

phaseCurves.label: Spitzer
phaseCurves.observed: a Spitzer IRAC 4.5 µm phase curve (program 11073, first published by Dang et al. (2018))

record.source: Bell et al. (2021), MNRAS 504, 3316, 'A comprehensive reanalysis of Spitzer's 4.5 um phase curves, and the phase variations of the ultra-hot Jupiters MASCARA-1b and KELT-16b' (doi:10.1093/mnras/stab1027; arXiv:2010.00687). Spitzer IRAC 4.5 um phase curve of CoRoT-2b, program 11073, first published by Dang et al. (2018) and reanalysed here. Values read from the authors' LaTeX source: the table of preferred SPCA model parameters (tab:preferred), row CoRoT-2b, detector model Poly4. The preferred fit is first order (the caption of its figure names the mode Poly4_v1), so the printed semi-amplitude and offset are the whole phase variation (section 4.1: semi-amplitude sqrt(C1^2 + D1^2), offset east -arctan2(D1, C1)). CoRoT-2 is one of the three systems the paper corrects for a nearby star's light (section 4.1, Dilution Correction; tab:dilution gives C_corr = 1.2046 for CoRoT-2, applied to the radius ratio as sqrt(C_corr) and to the dayside flux as C_corr); tab:preferred does not say in its caption that its cells carry the correction.

model.equation: F_p = F_day [1 + C1 (cos psi - 1) + D1 sin psi], psi counted from mid-eclipse (section 4.1), printed as its semi-amplitude and the offset east of its maximum.
